question: On 19 October 2026, following the 17 October protests across France, several prefects and competent authorities announced the introduction of curfews. The locations affected include Paris, Lille, Douai and Bordeaux, a list that is likely to grow in the coming days.

These decisions infringe a fundamental principle of the European Union: freedom of movement, which is enshrined in particular in Article 21 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU). They hinder the organisation of peaceful demonstrations and gatherings aimed at expressing anger at the social and economic situation in the country. In view of the above: 1.
Will the Commission ask the French authorities for clarification on how these curfews are being implemented, and will it monitor them?

Will it remind the French authorities that restrictions on the freedom of movement of EU citizens, as guaranteed by Article 21 TFEU, must comply with EU law, in particular the principles of necessity and proportionality?
